Mrs Tinubu made the call on Saturday at the South-East zonal APC Women Presidential Rally in Enugu, where she assured supporters that the President remained committed to transforming the country.
Addressing the gathering, the First Lady in a statement by her media aide , Busola Kukoyi,likened the challenges associated with the administration’s reforms to the pains of childbirth, saying the difficult period was over and the time had come for Nigerians to enjoy prosperity.
“As the President said, it is time for prosperity. You know, the pain of labour to birth a child is over. It is time for joy and prosperity,” she said.
She said Nigeria stood at the threshold of prosperity after enduring the pains of reforms, urging women in the region to rally behind President Tinubu’s second-term ambition.
The First Lady also assured that the President would not relent in his efforts to transform the country, describing the All Progressives Congress (APC) as a party that keeps its promises.
Mrs Tinubu highlighted the interventions of her Renewed Hope Initiative, which she said had consistently supported women, young people and vulnerable Nigerians through financial assistance, skills acquisition programmes and the distribution of equipment and working tools.
As part of the rally, she flagged off the distribution of empowerment items to 5,000 women in Enugu State.
The event attracted several political leaders from the South-East, including Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah; Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru; and Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma.
Also in attendance were the wives of the Senate President and Speaker of the House of Representatives, the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, the APC National Women Leader and the Minister of Women Affairs, alongside APC candidates seeking elective positions in the region.
Earlier, the First Lady and other women leaders visited the Enugu State Traditional Rulers Council, led by its Chairman, Igwe Samuel Asadu.
Speaking on behalf of the traditional rulers, Igwe Asadu expressed satisfaction with the achievements of the Tinubu administration and pledged their support for the President.
The traditional rulers also commended Mrs Tinubu for her efforts towards improving the welfare of women, youths and children through various interventions of the Renewed Hope Initiative.
